Away Tour
The tour leaves the morning Part Two drops. Six weeks abroad. You read the full contract on Vivaan's channel at the boarding gate, like everyone else in the country.
Tara. Your mother paid Vivaan. Your father showed me. I'm sorry I didn't say it last night.
...I know. Papa's nurse called me at 4 AM.
Thank you for going to see him. Nobody goes to see him.
The other side of the world. Rain. Every press conference is about the contract. Not one question about cricket.
Board's furious. Sponsors are dropping. And there's a TV anchor in the lobby who keeps "accidentally" getting in the lift with you.
Photos already. You, her, a lift. Captain, you are a disaster magnet.
Who is she?
No, don't answer. Clause seven. I have no right to ask.
...Who is she?
Call her. Right now. Explain.
Even if it's 3 AM there.

Short.
Text: "You're allowed to ask. Clause seven is dead."
Say it.
Two days later. A knock on your hotel door at midnight. Room service, you think.
Tara Kapoor. Soaked. No makeup. No security. No photographers. She took three flights.
I don't know anything about cricket. But I know what you look like when you're lying, and I know what you look like when you're tired. You look tired.
Tara Kapoor crossed the world without telling anyone. Not even Nikhil.
